title: GET: A Graph-Edge-Transport Framework for Device EDA and Visualization
content: Modern ultra-scaled-semiconductor-device design calls for simulation tools that connect electrical behavior to local charge and transport. In heterogeneous dielectrics, this requires identifying which charging location controls which leakage path, even when terminal current barely changes. We present Graph Edge Transport (GET), which couples current conservation, state occupations and Poisson electrostatics on a common graph for calculation and visualization. Branch-response maps link local interventions to current redistribution, retaining the identities of localized states and connections during electrostatic refinement or sparse sampling. In a dielectric calculation, reversing prescribed polarization changes the left-half current share from 81.25% to 17.23% while total current changes by only 0.0048%. An AlScN demonstration connects measured leakage to spatial conductivity control, with root mean square log-current errors of 0.0106 decades for fitting and 0.0194 decades at additional verification. GET reveals that in a localized-state device, polarization reverses the leakage response to added negative charge through competition between electrode supply and empty-state availability. The equilibrium resistor network and its minimum-resistance path miss the current enhancement. GET identifies the regions controlling leakage and determines the electrostatic resolution needed to analyze local interventions, which therefore paves the way to sub-1-nm node and advanced devices’ simulation.
